clue.text: More than one substitute quarrels about former post being withdrawn

the GPO, the General Post Office, was the old name of the British postal service

explanation.surface: Someone describes rows over an old postal job being abolished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' sets the old postal initials inside the quarrels, and 'being withdrawn' turns the resulting SPAGPOTS round. Post looks like mail or a job but means the Post Office.
explanation.definitionFit: Stopgaps are temporary replacements, so the plural matches more than one stand-in.

clue.text: Pigment in soap, I fancy?

indicators.note: fancy is used as an anagram signal, meaning elaborate or imaginative

explanation.definitionFit: Sinopia is a reddish-brown earth colour, used for underdrawings in fresco painting.

a fair is a show or exhibition

explanation.definitionFit: The Great Exhibition of 1851 was a world's fair held in London's Crystal Palace.

clue.text: Untouchable shock fed back by electronic system

explanation.walkthrough: Shock looks electrical, but it is a mass of hair; HAIR reverses to RIAH.
explanation.definitionFit: A pariah is an outcast; the word originally named a low Indian caste once called untouchables.

clue.text: Two chaps heading to east Bury?

indicators.note: the head, or first letter, of the pair travels to the east, the right-hand end of an across entry

Tom is a man's name, the other of the two chaps

explanation.surface: Two men set off for East Anglia's Bury St Edmunds, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: BENTOM has its first letter B moved to the end. The question mark warns that Bury, capitalised as the town, is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To entomb someone is to lay them in a tomb, a way of burying them.

clue.text: Almost too late lightning's destroyed part of London

indicators.note: the letters are wrecked and reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: Lightning has struck too late to stop the damage.
explanation.walkthrough: Fodder is TO (too cut short), LATE and LIGHTNING, the 's standing for is.
explanation.definitionFit: Notting Hill Gate is a district and Tube station in west London.

clue.text: Herb garden laid out in rings has died off

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go inside the two Os

parts.note: the letter O looks like a ring, so two rings give two Os

parts.note: d is the abbreviation for died, used in dates

explanation.surface: A herb garden's design is in circles, but the plants have perished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' drops the D, 'laid out' rearranges what remains into REGAN, and 'in' places that between the two rings.
explanation.definitionFit: Oregano is a culinary herb, wild marjoram, used in Italian cooking.

clue.text: Punching a short scientist that's no good

indicators.note: short means the last letter of the scientist is lopped off

parts.note: a boffin is British slang for a scientist

explanation.surface: A small, useless scientist hits someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To boff is informal for to hit, so boffing is striking with the fist.

clue.text: So going about mostly happy, otherwise gay

indicators.note: the Latin word goes around the rearranged letters

parts.note: sic is Latin for so or thus

indicators.note: otherwise means in another way, so the letters are rearranged
mostly means not quite all, so the last letter of the word happy goes

explanation.surface: Someone is fairly cheerful or otherwise light-hearted.
explanation.walkthrough: Gay seems to sit with happy, but it is the definition. 'mostly' trims the Y, 'otherwise' rearranges the rest, and 'going about' wraps the Latin word round them.
explanation.definitionFit: Sappho of Lesbos wrote love poems to women, so Sapphic describes lesbian love.

clue.text: Chemical that is not usually inert!

indicators.note: the letters are not in their usual order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark that a certain substance is normally reactive.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also works as a description: saltpetre is an ingredient of gunpowder, so hardly inert.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitre is potassium nitrate, a salt used in gunpowder and fertiliser.

clue.text: Scoff or criticise with complaint

parts.note: to roast someone is to criticise them harshly
a beef is a grumble or complaint

explanation.surface: Someone sneers or finds fault while moaning.
explanation.walkthrough: Scoff looks like a verb to mock, but here it is the British slang noun for food.
explanation.definitionFit: Scoff is informal British slang for food, and a joint of beef cooked in the oven is a classic meal.

clue.text: Hit on guide page that shows you what's on

explanation.definitionFit: A pilot lamp is a small indicator light showing that a device is switched on.

clue.text: Starts to interview Russian, asking questions in a foreign language

clue.text: A Year in Provence includes Times supplement

indicators.note: the French word holds the other letter inside it

parts.note: année is French for year, Provence being in France
the multiplication sign x is read as times

explanation.surface: A book review section prints Peter Mayle's memoir as a newspaper supplement.
explanation.walkthrough: A Year in Provence is Peter Mayle's bestselling memoir, and the Times is a British paper with supplements; both are decoys.
explanation.definitionFit: An annexe is an addition, either a building extension or an appendix added to a document.

clue.text: Film star Elvis gaining weight without working

parts.note: Elvis Presley was called the King of rock and roll

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the weight goes around the other piece

parts.note: kg is the abbreviation for kilogram, a weight
on means operating or working

explanation.definitionFit: The giant ape of the 1933 film is its title character and star.

clue.text: Endless chaos smashed a little shack up

indicators.note: smashed means broken up, so the letters are rearranged
the final letter of chaos is removed

parts.note: a bit means a little

explanation.surface: A wild, messy party wrecks a small hut.
explanation.walkthrough: CHAO, rearranged to COHA, is followed by BIT. Shack looks like a hut, but shack up is a phrasal verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean to live together as an unmarried couple.

clue.text: You're looking at this metal frame

parts.note: the solver is looking at a crossword grid
iron is a metal

explanation.surface: The clue points at the puzzle itself and calls it a metal framework.
explanation.definitionFit: A gridiron is a framework of parallel metal bars, used for grilling food over a fire.

clue.text: Refuse to spin idle gossip in English newspaper

indicators.note: to spin means to turn round, so the whole assembly is read backwards
the chatter goes inside the letters for English newspaper

parts.note: rag is slang for a poor-quality newspaper
gab is idle chatter

explanation.surface: Someone declines to put silly rumours in a British tabloid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the chatter after the E, giving EGABRAG, which 'to spin' turns round. Refuse looks like a verb but is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Refuse, stressed on the first syllable, is rubbish or waste.

clue.text: Current deputy head's beginning to welcome new comprehensive

indicators.note: to welcome means to take in, so the other letters hold the letter for new

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current
Chambers gives dept as an abbreviation for deputy

indicators.note: the beginning means the first letter of the word head

explanation.surface: A school's deputy head starts to greet a new comprehensive school pupil.
explanation.walkthrough: IDEPTH takes in N after the I. Comprehensive looks like the school, but it is an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: An in-depth study is thorough and covers everything in detail.

clue.text: Artist is thus with dry clothing

indicators.note: the two outer letters dress, or surround, the middle words

parts.note: TT, teetotal, means not drinking alcohol, i.e. dry
taken as written
so means thus, in this way

explanation.surface: A painter remarks on being parched while getting dressed.
explanation.definitionFit: James Tissot was a 19th-century French painter of fashionable society scenes.

clue.text: Self-harm makes son puke up uncontrollably

parts.note: to kid someone is to tease them
rap is a style of music

parts.note: Hair is a 1960s rock musical

explanation.definitionFit: Azure is a bright sky blue, the heraldic tincture for blue.

clue.text: A random number dividing an endless number that can't be seen in the lab
